description: Game Asset Source Verification Bypass The EC2 instance uses UserData scripts to download game assets from S3. If the S3 bucket name or path is compromised, or if the EC2 role permissions are too broad, an attacker could redirect asset loading to a malicious source. An attacker with access to the EC2 instance could modify the UserData script or environment variables to point to a different S3 bucket containing malicious game assets.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement strict S3 bucket policies and versioning controls

description: Unauthorized Stream Access Post-Authorization The current implementation validates authorization only at stream initiation through Cognito and API Gateway. Once WebRTC connection is established, there's no continuous validation of user authorization status. A user whose access has been revoked could continue using an active streaming session indefinitely if no periodic revalidation occurs.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material
recommendation: Implement periodic token refresh and validation

description: Instance Metadata Table Manipulation The DynamoDB table stores instance-to-user mappings and instance metadata. If compromised, an attacker could modify these mappings to redirect users to unauthorized or malicious instances. An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the status check Lambda function to inject malicious data into DynamoDB, redirecting users to an attacker-controlled server.
references: recommendation: Implement strict validation and verification for instance metadata
recommendation: Enhance monitoring and alerting for metadata changes

description: Pixel Stream Integrity Compromise WebRTC streams could be intercepted or modified in transit, especially if proper encryption and integrity checks are not implemented. An attacker performs a man-in-the-middle attack on the WebRTC stream, injecting malicious frames or modifying game content in real-time.
references: recommendation: Implement robust WebRTC security measures
recommendation: Add monitoring for stream integrity

description: Denial of Service Through Request Flooding Multiple clients could send a high volume of streaming requests simultaneously, overwhelming the request queue, matchmaker Lambda, or available EC2 instances. An attacker uses multiple accounts or a botnet to flood the system with streaming requests, depleting available resources and preventing legitimate users from accessing the service.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement comprehensive rate limiting and throttling
recommendation: Enhance resource management and scaling
recommendation: Add DDoS protection and monitoring
